subject: MerchantCo demo — recommended model shortlist & evaluation playbook
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Devon Reyes <devon@merchantco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantCo demo — recommended model shortlist & evaluation playbook

Hi Devon —

Thanks again for the demo time earlier. Per our conversation I pulled together a compact playbook (below) with three candidate inference options, the pragmatic tradeoffs we observed in the sandbox runs, and recommended next steps for a short QA sprint. Goal here: give your eng and data teams an operationally realistic way to validate quality vs latency/cost before procurement.

Quick TL;DR:
- Recommended shortlist (best starting points): rw-luma-7B-q4, open-13B-q8-light, falcon-40B-int8-prod-variant
- Runner-up for hallucination-sensitive flows: rw-luma-7B + strengthened prompt guardrails (lower cost, faster latency)
- For highest accuracy at the expense of cost: falcon-40B-int8 (worse throughput on a single GPU but stronger factuality on our retail prompts)

Benchmarks (sandbox, 512-token context):
- rw-luma-7B-q4 — median p95 latency: 180 ms / token; tokens/sec per GPU: ~65; cost estimate: low
- open-13B-q8-light — median p95 latency: 320 ms / token; tokens/sec per GPU: ~34; cost estimate: medium
- falcon-40B-int8-prod-variant — median p95 latency: 720 ms / token; tokens/sec per GPU: ~12; cost estimate: high

Key quality notes from the demo prompts:
- On product-description generation (canonicalization + attribute extraction) rw-luma-7B was competitive on style but missed rare numerical attributes ~8% of cases.
- open-13B-q8-light reduced omission errors vs 7B (particularly on multilingual titles) but introduced occasional verbosity that needs a tighter decoding/prompt setup.
- falcon-40B-int8 had the strongest factual recall on long-tail SKUs and reduced hallucinations the most, but at meaningful cost/latency tradeoffs.

Ask/next steps I propose:
1) Short QA sprint (2 weeks) — we supply: 1) a 1000-example prompt set (covering core SKU types), 2) a prompt variants pack, 3) benchmark harness + our sandbox runner. You run locally or we can run on Redwood Dedicated.
2) Quick calibration call for your infra team to pick the deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated) — I recommend Dedicated if you plan >100 qps sustained.
3) Procurement checkpoint — if results look good we’ll hand over SOW draft and an expected monthly T-shirt cost based on selected model and batching profiles.

I attached the bench CSV and the prompt set we used. I also included a one-page SOW draft to accelerate procurement if your legal/procurement want to start reviewing.

If helpful, we can spin a short canary that wires the 7B and 13B candidates into one endpoint with split routing so your product team can AB the UX without shifting contracts.

Open items I want to flag now:
- Regression monitoring: we should agree on a small run of golden prompts (20–30 checks) and an automatic regression alert if quality drops >5% on those.
- Prompt locking: any live production routing should include an immutable prompt layer to prevent drift during rollout.

Available this week for a 30-min calibration call. What’s your team’s availability?

Thanks —
Irene

Thanks, Irene — super clear. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side:

1) For the 1000-example set you mentioned, will you label expected outputs or just provide prompts + gold inputs? Our QA team prefers expected outputs for the golden checks.
2) You called out the RW-7B omission rate (~8%) — can you share a couple of representative examples where it missed numeric attributes? That will help our PMs see the gap.
3) On the Dedicated recommendation — can you ballpark the monthly committed cost for a 3-GPU pool running the 13B at 60 qps? Procurement wants a rough number before we commit to the sprint.

We’re available Tue/Wed morning PST for the calibration call.

—Devon

On Sep 9, 2028, at 2:03 PM, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick TL;DR:
> - Recommended shortlist (best starting points): rw-luma-7B-q4, open-13B-q8-light, falcon-40B-int8-prod-variant

Thanks for the clear write-up, Irene. Devon — quick answers while we set up the calibration call:  

1) Prompt set — we can provide both: the prompts + expected outputs for the golden set (labels for ~200 golden checks) and the broader 1k unlabeled prompts for load and edge-case coverage. We usually include an annotation guide so your QA can score outputs consistently.

2) Representative misses from rw-luma-7B-q4 (two examples copied from the sandbox):
- SKU 98421: prompt asked to extract "net_weight" — model returned "weight: light" (missed numeric 2.3).
- SKU 34112: asked to canonicalize "color" from messy title — model returned generic "blue" instead of "navy blue" (loss of specificity).

Irene/Devon: we recommend running the 7B first for latency-sensitive endpoints (search autosuggest, short generative blurbs) and use the 13B for tasks requiring better recall (attribute extraction, multilingual title normalization). If hallucination/factuality matters a lot, run the 40B gated behind a verification step (e.g., candidate-generation from 40B + fast verification with 13B).

3) Cost ballpark for a 3-GPU Dedicated pool (13B q8 light): monthly committed cost estimate ~ $28k–$36k depending on reserved hours and burst policies. We’ll include a clearer cost table in the SOW with batching assumptions.

Ben — can you drop the exact sandbox examples and the bench CSV into the shared link? Monica — can you confirm if we can provide a one-week hosted sandbox for MerchantCo so they can run initial checks without a Dedicated commit?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference

4) Open gating items for procurement:

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
